candidates.trigger: ZDLov-1F (Uradni list 28/2025, in force 26 Apr 2025): mandatory marking of ungulates at harvest, new damaged-party records, two-year ground planning; new rulebook on marking harvested ungulates and recording game after harvest (Uradni list 2025-01-2805).
candidates.unchecked: Rulebook obligations and deadlines; whether a state e-system (for example from the hunting institute) already takes the records; number of hunting families; whether they pay for software. No competitor search run, search budget exhausted.

candidates.buyer: Horse keepers, riding clubs, small stables

candidates.evidence: https://www.gov.si/drzavni-organi/organi-v-sestavi/uprava-za-varno-hrano-veterinarstvo-in-varstvo-rastlin (search summary only; unclear whether the rule is in force or in preparation)

candidates.unchecked: Whether the rule is adopted and its date; whether Volos will carry equid reporting; size of buyer base. Free state portal probably kills it.

candidates.trigger: ZPPDFT-2: enter beneficial owner in AJPES eRDL within 8 days of registration and of each change; filing requires a qualified e-signature and e-authorisation; supervisors still find late filers; public access limited since Aug 2025.
candidates.unchecked: Penalties actually applied; volume of unfiled associations; AJPES annual-report duties for associations not checked.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: One search; only public/subsidised home-care programmes and unrelated results, no household-employer-specific duty or product found. Nothing actionable; unverified whether a registration or reporting duty exists beyond normal employer registration.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Collectors need ARSO collector registration, keep collection records 3 years, annual report to ARSO by 31 March, evidenčni list per shipment: nothing new beyond K07. No Slovenian cash-payment ban for scrap found (only Croatia, Czechia have one).

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: One combined search with cat 4 returned nothing specific on Slovenian second-hand or pawn record duties. Unverified; no candidate.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: No Slovenian-specific licensing or purchase-register rule found; only metrology office warnings about scales and old press on buyers. Nothing actionable; ZPPDFT-2 duties for precious-metal buyers unchecked.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Destruction certificate (potrdilo o razgradnji) rulebook dates from 2010; free dismantling at authorised plants; no new register or deadline found. Nothing new beyond K07.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Movements via free UVHVVR Volos portal and TRACES; EIRŽ register. New animal health law implementing rules from Aug 2026 add mandatory movement reporting and holding registration for equids (horse stables, riding clubs) - see equid candidate. Trader-specific duties not found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: No search spent; budget used on water, waste and agro-dealer leads.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K13.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K08; vet-medicine sellers not searched separately.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water-right holders must meter abstraction and report volumes electronically by end of January using Excel templates sent by e-mail to Direkcija RS za vode; implementing regulation still pending; inspectorate checked borehole use in agriculture in Sept 2025; Aug 2026 drought call to limit abstractions in Pomurje. One candidate raised.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: New ZOPVOOV (in force 1 Apr 2025) and Uredba on municipal wastewater; owners of small treatment plants (MKČN) need first measurements and operational monitoring by an authorised contractor (every 3 years under 200 PE); 2022 ARSO review found irregularities at 178 operators; gov.si says unified rules come in 2026 and no fines in 2026. One candidate raised.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Pressure equipment periodic inspections by ministry-authorised accredited bodies (rulebook 92/2008) with stickers and certificates; lifts in multi-flat buildings were a 2023 housing-inspectorate action. Owner-side tracking is a generic asset-inspection tool; weak candidate only.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K12.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: New FFS trade rulebook (Uradni list 6/2026, applies from 14 Feb 2026) on trade conditions and keeping and sending trade data; distributors send annual sales data to UVHVVR by 31 March; retail needs a card-holding seller and a part-time advisor. Applicator spray records are K02. One distributor candidate raised.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Temporary-work agencies registered with the labour ministry, 30,000 EUR bank guarantee, annual report by 31 March, 8-day change notice. Small buyer pool; weak.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: ZPPDej (2016, amended 2022): cemetery operators keep grave plans, burial books and lease/payment records; funeral permits in ministry register. Municipal/utility-run, no 2025 change found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Associations (društva), institutes and co-operatives must enter beneficial owner in AJPES eRDL within 8 days of registration and of any change; public access restricted since Aug 2025; supervisors still find late filers. Free state portal; weak candidate. Halal and kosher not searched.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Draft amendment to the Road Transport Act put to consultation 30 Sep 2026 (comments to 13 Oct): optional taximeter, app invoices, new rental-with-driver class, A1 Slovene test. Still a proposal. Trucking and bus fleets not searched.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers (menjalci) licensed by Bank of Slovenia, public register 2025; AML reporting duties not confirmed. Market and street traders not searched.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Hunting: ZDLov-1F (in force 26 Apr 2025) and a 2025 rulebook require marking of ungulates at harvest and recording game after harvest. Farm supplementary activities: income report to the administrative unit by 31 March, including zero income. Tattoo studios, driving schools and nurseries not reached.

(EU) 2024/573 and the Slovenian decree on F-gases and ODS: a per-unit Evidenca o opremi filled in at every intervention, copy kept by the servicer at least 5 years, equipment registration and annual reporting through ARSO REMIS_TGP. candidates.trigger: ZDOsk-1 / ZDOsk-1A (OG 112/24): RIDO registration (Pravilnik OG 46/2025), quality and safety system with analysis and reporting, coordinator duties (visit frequency by care category, notices to ZZZS and entry point, assistance with family-carer monthly reports). ZZZS pays flat daily rates per user for 1 Dec 2025 to 30 Sep 2026.
candidates.unchecked: Whether ZZZS or the ministry mandates or provides an IT portal or data interface for visits and billing; number and size of providers; whether rates and rules are stable after 30 Sep 2026; existing nursing-home or home-care software vendors.

candidates.buyer: Private apartment owners and room renters (sobodajalci) letting short term, especially in high-risk municipalities.
candidates.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals / 34
candidates.existing: AJPES eTurizem and the register of accommodation facilities (the state tool that killed K06). Competitor search (ZGos-1 register ID kratkotrajni najem) found no software.
candidates.name: Short-term rental compliance pack under ZGos-1 (ID number, consents, day cap)
candidates.trigger: ZGos-1 (OG 77/25): register entry and mandatory ID number linked to the cadastre, owner and co-owner consents (over 3/4 of shares, neighbours; valid 3 years), day caps (60 days default in high-risk municipalities, municipal caps 30-270; sobodajalec cap 180 days per Portorož presentation), sticker, inspections. Decree on high-risk municipalities adopted 16 Apr 2026. Effective date not confirmed.
candidates.unchecked: Entry-into-force dates, who issues the ID, whether platforms or AJPES count days, and whether consents and day counts need any tool beyond a form. A one-off registration deadline could be a trigger but was not found.

candidates.unchecked: Competitor software; whether the work is software or just consultancy; number of practices; willingness to pay.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Nothing new. Only duty found is the ministerial order requiring distributors to report retail price changes per station (Price Control Act) and the station technical-requirements rulebook (consolidated 1 Jun 2022). Buyers are mostly large distributors. No 2025 register or evidence duty found for small operators.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Only market-information reporting to ARSKTRP: 2024 rulebook on the grain/oilseed market (price and quantity reporting above 500 t/yr of wheat and maize, stock reporting above 1,000 t/yr) and milk first-buyer monthly reporting (by the 20th). Thresholds push this toward larger firms and reporting goes through a state portal. Logged as a weak candidate.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Zakon o zadrugah novela (2021): auditor (revizor) institute, special-purpose co-operatives, annual report to AJPES within 8 months under a special accounting standard. Nothing new for software; no 2024-27 rule found.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes

coverage.found: No Slovenian source found on pharmacy duties for drug precursors (search returned Slovak pages only, discarded). UPPD issued guidelines on 10 Jun 2024 and ZNPosr was amended (OG 76/25). Accountants and tax advisers (about 5,000 entities per ZDSS, 2022) also fall under ZPPDFT-2. No notary-specific reporting found. Logged as a weak candidate.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Guest register and tax duty is K06 (rejected, eTurizem). New: Zakon o gostinstvu ZGos-1 (OG 77/25) sets an ID number and a register entry for short-term rentals, owner and co-owner consents (valid 3 years) and day caps. Mandatory categorisation of 4-5 star and farm-tourism lodgings. Logged as a weak candidate related to K06.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Budget. EUDR timber is already K01. Intrastat thresholds were raised from 1 Jan 2026, which reduces reporting. CBAM, fish and food export certificates not searched.

coverage.category: 31. F-gas and ozone-depleting-substance servicers and equipment operators (country-specific)
coverage.found: Authorised companies must keep an equipment record (Evidenca o opremi) for each unit of 5 t CO2e or more (3 kg for ODS) and report via ARSO REMIS_TGP. Reg. 2024/573 and new certificate rules (2024/2215, 2025/625, 2025/1893) apply. The Inspectorate checked 223 firms in 2024. One candidate logged.

coverage.category: 32. Long-term care (dolgotrajna oskrba) providers under ZDOsk (country-specific, law in force 2025-26)
coverage.found: Providers must be in the RIDO register (Pravilnik OG 46/2025). ZDOsk-1A (OG 112/24) adds quality-system, analysis and reporting duties. ZZZS pays a flat daily rate per user from 1 Dec 2025 to 30 Sep 2026. Coordinators must visit users on a set schedule (monthly for categories 4-5) and report. One candidate logged.

coverage.category: 33. Medical and dental X-ray users (radiation permits) (country-specific)
coverage.found: URSVS permits for radiation activity and source use, a radiation-protection assessment valid 10 years (a generic dental assessment is valid to 23 May 2028), annual device inspection report by ZVD, and notice within 15 days of ceasing use. One weak candidate logged.

coverage.category: 34. Short-term accommodation lettings under ZGos-1 (country-specific)
coverage.found: See category 29. The government decree on high-risk municipalities was adopted 16 Apr 2026. EU Reg. 2024/1028 (STR) is applicable in most provisions from 20 May 2026 (from memory, unverified).

coverage.category: 35. Agricultural first buyers: milk, grain and oilseed market reporting to ARSKTRP (country-specific)
coverage.found: See category 22. Monthly electronic reporting to the ARSKTRP portal. Thresholds mean mostly mid-size and large firms.

coverage.category: 36. AML-obliged small professional offices: accountants, tax advisers, estate agents (country-specific, ZPPDFT-2)
coverage.found: See category 28. Only paid training seminars found (racunovodja.com). Official UPPD pages not opened.

coverage.category: 37. Sole-trader (s.p.) tax regime changes 2026: normiranci and ZIURS (country-specific)
coverage.found: New 2026 flat-rate tax rules and a new minimum contribution base from 1 Jul 2026 are tax and accounting changes, not a recurring register or report to an authority, so they are generic accounting. Intrastat threshold increases reduce, not add, duties.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Slaughterhouses and cutting plants need UVHVVR approval under Reg 853/2004 (gov.si 'Odobritev živilskega obrata'); retail butchers register under the Pravilnik o registraciji in odobritvi obratov na področju živil. No Slovenian butcher-specific software vendor found (searched HACCP, lot traceability, POS). The one live duty is origin traceability for unpackaged fresh beef, pork, sheep, goat and poultry (Pravilnik, Ur.l. RS 54/2022): origin on the delivery note or invoice, applying since 30 Oct 2023, and the SI marking on the retail receipt for Slovenian-origin counter meat. That receipt deadline was extended from 31 Oct 2025 to 31 Oct 2027 (Ur.l. RS 76/2025, 3 Oct 2025). UVHVVR's extraordinary inspection of 21 Aug 2026 found the supermarket butcher counters clean. Irregularities were at 3 of 7 suppliers (slaughterhouses and cutting plants): lot separation, record-keeping and lot quantity mismatches, and misuse of the 'Izbrana kakovost' label. A government working group (formed 29 Feb 2024) is preparing a state electronic system to track meat mass flow by origin. It has no launch date, which would be a future trigger but also a risk of a free state tool. Counts of small abattoirs and butchers not found. The ~69-butcher inspection with 47 failing is about 2015, so not current.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Timber/EUDR is already K01. Intrastat is not worth a candidate (thresholds raised from 1 Jan 2026, per the assignment). CBAM: full phase from 1 Jan 2026; authorised declarant status is required for imports of steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity above 50 t per year. First annual declaration is due 30 Sep 2027. FURS has a CBAM calculator (Mar 2026) and a CBAM page, and customs brokers and forwarders (DHL, Unija) sell the declarant service. Small importers under 50 t are exempt, so the buyer pool is thin and served. Fish: the EU CATCH system for IUU catch certificates has been mandatory for importers since 10 Jan 2026 (FURS guidance 9/2024), and CATCH is a free EU tool. Plants and wood: exporters and importers must be in the FITO register. Electronic phytosanitary certificates have been issued since 1 Apr 2024 through TRACES (free). From 6 Jul 2026 some import certificates need an additional declaration. Veterinary export certificates: the exporter notifies the UVHVVR regional vet at least 3 working days ahead on a form template, and the certificate is issued by an official vet, with no e-service found. Organic imports: COI in TRACES, importers registered with UVHVVR/MKGP. All are state or EU portals or small buyer pools. China poultry and pork export audit status (early 2025) not confirmed.

result.competitor: Only the free state Excel templates (one is a macro .xlsm), with no portal. Searches for software or a service that prepares the report, or links telemetry meter reading to it, found no private provider. Hydrogeology firms prepare permit reports, but none was found offering the annual abstraction report. Utilities use remote meter reading for their own metering, but none was found tied to DRSV reporting. A future state portal under the pending regulation is a possible risk; its status is unverified.
result.duty: Zakon o vodah (ZV-1): water-right holders must meter how much water they take and report it electronically to MNVP, in a way the minister is to set by regulation. That regulation has not been adopted (no 2026 pravilnik found), so for now the permit or concession sets the terms. DRSV asks for an annual report with a chart of volumes by end of January for the previous year, using its Excel templates (wells, intakes, springs with Qes), sent by e-mail to gp.drsv@gov.si or by post. Penalty: no specific fine amount found. IRSNR inspections in 2025 led to 4 orders to fix problems, 1 misdemeanour decision with a warning and 3 warnings, all about use beyond or without a permit. An earlier drinking-water inspection campaign produced 35 decisions, including orders to install meters.
result.market: Not well measured. ARSO counts from 2008 (about 18 years old): 20,443 permits for self-supply, 11,521 for watering, 169 for irrigation, 288 for process water. A Feb 2026 MNVP press pack seems to cite about 2,782 water-charge payers, including about 1,151 for electricity production. That figure is second-hand: it came from a search summary because the .docx could not be read. How many holders actually have a metering and reporting condition in their permit is not_reached. A realistic paying segment (greenhouses, fish farms, small hydro, groundwater heat pumps) is probably in the low thousands at most.
result.reason: The duty is real. Under ZV-1, water-right holders must meter how much water they take and report it electronically to the ministry. The minister's rule on how to report still has not been adopted (no 2026 pravilnik found), so for now each permit sets the terms. The Direkcija RS za vode (DRSV) asks for a report with a chart of the volumes by end of January, using free state Excel templates. No portal exists and no private provider was found. Still, the job is small: one Excel sheet a year built from meter readings. No specific fine was found. Recent inspections focused on use that exceeds or lacks a permit, not on missing reports. The one misdemeanour case found ended with a warning, not a fine. Buyers are scattered, hard to reach and unlikely to pay. A stronger angle would be selling it bundled with telemetry meters.

result.duty:
The duty is real and in force. It comes from the Slovenian Uredba o uporabi fluoriranih toplogrednih plinov in ozonu škodljivih snoveh (Ur. l. RS 60/2016; consolidated text dated 1.1.2025 on tax-fin-lex), applied alongside Reg. (EU) 2024/573.
- Equipment registration (Art. 4): operators must register stationary equipment holding 3 kg or more within 3 months of installation, and report changes within 1 month, via REMIS_TGP.
- Annual report (Art. 7): authorised companies, mobile/car-AC maintainers, in-house users with their own servicer, and gas sellers report by 31 March for the previous year. A nil report is required. Submission is through the ARSO REMIS web form.
- Equipment record (Evidenca o opremi): kept per unit of 5 t CO2e or more. The servicer fills it in at every intervention; the operator keeps the original and the servicer keeps a copy for at least 5 years.
- Penalties: I could not see fine amounts; the penal articles were not in the fetched text. Enforcement is real but soft. In the 2024 action, IRSOE found violations at 135 of 223 firms and opened 83 misdemeanour cases, which ended in 54 reminders and 19 warnings with no fines yet.
- Not checked: whether REMIS accepts file import; the obligations PDF for authorised companies.
result.market: Small, roughly a few hundred servicing firms; I found no exact count of the register. Only for non-reporting in 2022, ARSO's list held 157 authorised firms, 64 car-AC maintainers and 2 traders, and 24 of these no longer existed. The total register of authorised companies is probably a few hundred to around 1,000. Operators of 5 t CO2e or more equipment (shops, hotels, offices) are more numerous but uncounted, and they rely on their servicer to fill in the record.
result.reason: The duty is real and recurring: a record entry at every intervention and an annual report by 31 March. No local software does the job. But the market is tiny, likely a few hundred servicers. The annual report is a short free state web form, so it causes little pain. Enforcement mostly produces reminders and warnings rather than fines. Many servicers already have job-sheet or ERP habits, so willingness to pay for a narrow F-gas logbook is probably low. A per-unit digital logbook plus report pre-fill is a simple MVP, and distribution through the training providers (SPOT list) and refrigerant wholesalers is possible. But revenue potential in Slovenia alone is too small unless it is bundled into a broader HVAC field-service product or sold across the region.

result.competitor: No Slovenian commercial app for home-care DO visit logging or ZZZS DO billing turned up in four Slovenian-language vendor searches. Two things already cover parts of the job. First, ZZZS has its own IT support for e-oskrba contracts, price lists, personal plans and home-care billing, with uploads through the ZZZS provider portal and web service; it also built a temporary Excel tool with built-in checks. Second, the ministry says it is building an IT solution in phases and is considering a new public tender. Nova Vizija's ProMedica community-nursing mobile app is an adjacent product. The nursing homes are already reported to be using upgraded in-house or vendor software. I did not reach any specific vendor names for software used by homes for the elderly (DSO) or by home-help providers.
result.duty: Real and in force. ZDOsk-1 as amended by ZDOsk-1A (OG 112/2024, applies from 28 Dec 2024) requires providers to be entered in RIDO, which NIJZ keeps (Pravilnik OG 46/2025). Providers bill ZZZS by electronic XML exchange: the ZZZS technical instruction for DO billing is at V1.2 (17 Dec 2025), the shipment-exchange web service at V1.4 (19 Mar 2026), and the provider manual at V1.1 (17 Jun 2026). Billing is monthly. Rejected submissions mean no payment, and ZZZS runs administrative and professional supervision. On 18 Sep 2026 the government adopted temporary measures. They extend the transitional financing method based on the DO billing day to end-2027, scrap the recommended-services plan and simplify changes to personal plans. Flat-rate or day-based billing therefore continues past 30 Sep 2026, which lowers the need for visit-level billing logic. I did not find the specific penalty amounts.
result.market: Very small. In October 2025, 120 municipalities had contracts with 39 home-care DO providers. ZZZS lists 117 DO providers and e-oskrba suppliers in total. There are 102 homes for the elderly, which care for about 20,042 institutional users and are mostly public bodies or concessionaires. About 4,500 home-care decisions had been issued by spring 2026. Many providers are public institutes (centres for social work, homes for the elderly, municipal home-help institutes) that buy through public procurement, not small private firms.
result.reason: The duty is real and recurring: monthly XML billing to ZZZS, RIDO registration and personal plans. No dedicated commercial Slovenian tool was found. But the buyer group is tiny (about 39 home-care providers and 117 DO/e-oskrba entities), and most are public institutes that buy through procurement. ZZZS already provides a portal, a web service and an Excel tool, and the ministry is building a state IT system. The rules are unstable: the 18 Sep 2026 temporary measures extend flat billing-day financing to end-2027 and cut planning paperwork, so a visit-to-billing engine has less to do. Integrating with the ZZZS XML format is feasible but specialised. Willingness to pay and distribution are weak for a solo founder.

Duty is real but mostly fragmented. The under-50-PE register reporting is confirmed: public utilities (izvajalci GJS) report to ARSO by 31 March via an Excel macro form (Obrazec MKCN 2025) emailed to gp.arso-vode@gov.si. Larger plants have per-permit monitoring, mostly every 2 years (examples at 100, 350, 650, 900 PE), annual at about 1000 PE, with annual ARSO reports. This differs from the claim's tiering. A 2026 systemic reform is promised and there are no fines in 2026. Operator count not found. I found no dedicated software, but I searched only briefly. The buyer set is tiny, the contractor does the measuring, and the cycle is slow. The claim's cited 2025-12-31 gov.si page confirms only the 2026 reform and no-fines point. The ZOPVOOV 1 Apr 2025 date and the 3/2/1-year tiers were not verified.

The duty is real. The Pravilnik (Uradni list RS 80/2025) applies from 1 May 2026. Hunting-ground managers must tag ungulates with a tamper-proof tag (vezica) before moving them. They must keep electronic logbooks of kills and losses, scanning the tag code and entering the data by the time the animal reaches a collection point. The text I read states no fines. The state side looks covered: Zavod za gozdove issues the tags free and keeps the tag list electronically. The rulebook names no specific app, and my searches found no commercial or state recording app, so I could not confirm who supplies the logbook software. I did not find a register count of hunting families. The buyers are volunteer associations with low willingness to pay, and a state or hunting-association tool likely exists or will be supplied. The one-off 2026 deadline has already passed. The rulebook's 17 October 2025 publication date also differs from the claim's 2025-01-2805 identifier and its ZDLov-1F date, which I did not reconcile.
